**Keyword:** Green Energy

**Status:** Milestones 0–4 completed. This page is a project overview for review, not the final report.

[Open the Milestone 4 presentation](presentation.qmd)

## Project topic

We compare renewable-energy adoption, renewable electricity sources, economic context, and changes since 2000 across contrasting national energy systems.

**Selected countries:** Germany, Denmark, Norway, France, China, United States, India, Brazil, Japan, and South Africa.

## Data source

[Our World in Data Energy Dataset](https://github.com/owid/energy-data), prepared reproducibly from the saved source snapshot in `data/energy_source/`.

The working dataset covers 2000–2025. Renewable primary-energy shares are available through 2024, electricity indicators through 2025, and GDP through 2022. Missing values are preserved; the economic comparison uses the common year 2022. The requested source is now a legacy release and is no longer updated.

## Target audience

A general, non-expert audience interested in sustainability, renewable energy, and global development.

## Main insights

1. Renewable-energy adoption differs greatly across countries.
2. Countries follow different renewable-energy pathways.
3. Economic size does not automatically determine renewable-energy leadership.
4. Countries have made very different gains in renewable-energy share since 2000.

## Main prioritized insight

**There is no single path to renewable energy. Countries differ in how much renewable energy they use, which renewable sources they rely on, and how their renewable-energy shares have changed over time.**

## Review materials

The three Python notebooks in `notebooks/` cover data preparation, main insights, and four visual drafts. The reviewed figures are in `visuals/`; the presentation connects them into the Milestone 4 story.

The final report and 3D visualization are future work.
